title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
plain: The computer checks the resistance of the heater inside each oxygen sensor. The heater in the downstream (after the catalytic converter) sensor on bank 2 measured outside its normal range.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
May fail an emissions or readiness test

causes.name: Worn or failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Wrong or aftermarket sensor with a different heater rating
High resistance from a corroded connector or damaged wiring

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Measure the heater resistance and compare to spec
Make sure any replacement sensor is the correct part for the vehicle
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor of the correct type.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: The computer checks the resistance of the heater inside each oxygen sensor. The heater in the third, furthest-downstream sensor on bank 2 measured outside its normal range.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
May fail an emissions or readiness test

causes.name: Worn or failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Wrong or aftermarket sensor with a different heater rating
High resistance from a corroded connector or damaged wiring

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Measure the heater resistance and compare to spec
Make sure any replacement sensor is the correct part for the vehicle
fix: Usually a new oxygen sensor of the correct type.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
plain: Oxygen sensors have a built-in heater so they start working soon after a cold start. The computer found a fault, such as an open circuit, in the heater circuit of the third, furthest-downstream oxygen sensor on bank 2.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Failed heater inside the oxygen sensor
Blown fuse for the oxygen sensor heaters
Damaged or melted wiring near the exhaust

checks: Check the oxygen sensor heater fuse
Inspect the sensor wiring for melted or rubbed-through spots near the exhaust
Measure the heater resistance at the sensor and compare to spec
fix: Most often a new oxygen sensor. If the fuse is blown, find the short that blew it before replacing the sensor.

symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Range/Performance
plain: Some engines blow a small stream of air past the fuel injectors to break the fuel into a finer mist. The computer found that the control for this air-assist system is not working the way it should.
symptoms: Possible rough idle or hesitation, mostly when cold

causes.name: Carbon buildup in the air passages

checks: Inspect the air-assist hoses and valve
Check the valve wiring and connector
fix: Usually repairing a leaking hose or replacing the air-assist control valve.

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit or Circuit Low
plain: Some engines blow a small stream of air past the fuel injectors to break the fuel into a finer mist. The computer found that the control for this air-assist system has a circuit fault or low voltage.
symptoms: Possible rough idle or hesitation, mostly when cold

causes.name: Faulty air-assist control valve or solenoid

checks: Inspect the air-assist hoses and valve
Check the valve wiring and connector
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new air-assist control valve.

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit High
plain: Some engines blow a small stream of air past the fuel injectors to break the fuel into a finer mist. The computer found that the control for this air-assist system has a voltage that is too high.
symptoms: Possible rough idle or hesitation, mostly when cold

causes.name: Faulty air-assist control valve or solenoid

checks: Inspect the air-assist hoses and valve
Check the valve wiring and connector
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new air-assist control valve.

title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
plain: The computer compares how much air the engine is taking in (from the MAF or MAP sensor) with how far the throttle is open. Those readings do not agree, so it suspects an air leak or a bad sensor.
symptoms: Hesitation or stalling, especially when slowing down

causes.name: Vacuum or intake air leak after the throttle
Dirty or faulty mass air flow (MAF) sensor
Dirty or failing electronic throttle body
Faulty MAP sensor or cracked MAP hose
Wiring problem at the throttle body or MAF sensor

checks: Check intake hoses, PCV hose and vacuum lines for cracks or leaks
Inspect and clean the MAF sensor and throttle body
Compare MAF, MAP and throttle readings at idle and under load with a scan tool
fix: Often fixing a vacuum leak or cleaning the throttle body and MAF sensor. If that fails, a new throttle body or MAF sensor.

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Barometric Pressure Correlation
plain: With the engine off or at key-on, the pressure in the intake manifold should match the outside air pressure. The computer found that the manifold pressure and barometric pressure readings do not agree.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or rough running

causes.name: Faulty barometric pressure sensor (sometimes built into another sensor or the computer)
Clogged, cracked or disconnected MAP sensor hose

checks: Compare MAP and barometric readings with the key on and engine off
Inspect the MAP sensor hose and port for blockage
fix: Usually a new MAP sensor, or clearing a blocked hose or port.

title: MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation (Bank 1)
plain: The computer compares the manifold pressure sensor with the mass air flow sensor. Their readings for bank 1 do not agree, which usually means an air leak or a bad sensor.
checks: Look for cracked intake hoses and vacuum leaks
Clean or test the MAF sensor
Compare MAP and MAF readings with a scan tool
fix: Usually fixing an air leak or replacing the MAF or MAP sensor.

title: MAP - Exhaust Pressure Correlation
plain: Mostly on diesels, the computer compares intake manifold pressure with exhaust pressure. The two readings do not line up the way they should.

causes.name: Clogged or cracked exhaust pressure sensor tube
Faulty MAP or boost pressure sensor

checks: Inspect the exhaust pressure sensor tube for soot clogging or cracks
Compare both sensor readings with the engine off
fix: Often cleaning or replacing the exhaust pressure sensor tube, or a new sensor.

title: MAP - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation
plain: The computer compares intake manifold pressure with the pressure at the turbo or supercharger inlet. The readings do not agree when they should.

causes.name: Faulty MAP or boost pressure sensor
Intake leak or blocked air filter

checks: Compare both pressure readings with the engine off, when they should match
Check the air filter and intake ducts
fix: Usually a new inlet pressure or MAP sensor, or an intake repair.

title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation
plain: With the engine off, the pressure at the turbo or supercharger inlet should match the outside air pressure. The computer found that these two readings do not agree.
checks: Compare both readings with the key on and engine off
Inspect the sensor connectors and wiring
fix: Usually replacing whichever sensor reads wrong.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control "A" Supply Voltage Circuit Low
plain: The "A" boost control actuator needs a steady power supply to work. The computer found that the supply voltage to it is too low.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Blown fuse or failed relay for the actuator

checks: Check the fuse and relay feeding the actuator
Measure supply voltage at the actuator connector
Inspect the wiring harness for damage
fix: Usually a fuse, relay or wiring repair; sometimes a new boost actuator.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control "A" Supply Voltage Circuit High
plain: The "A" boost control actuator needs a steady power supply to work. The computer found that the supply voltage to it is too high.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Power wire shorted to another voltage source
Charging system putting out too much voltage

checks: Check the fuse and relay feeding the actuator
Measure supply voltage at the actuator connector
Inspect the wiring harness for damage
fix: Usually a fuse, relay or wiring repair; sometimes a new boost actuator.

title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit
plain: The outside air temperature sensor, usually behind the front grille or bumper, tells the computer how warm it is outside. The computer found a fault in the circuit.
symptoms: Wrong outside temperature on the dash
Automatic climate control may not work right

causes.name: Damaged sensor, often from road debris or a minor front-end hit
Broken or corroded wiring behind the bumper

checks: Check the dash outside temperature reading against the real temperature
Inspect the sensor and its wiring behind the grille or bumper
Test the sensor resistance at a known temperature
fix: Usually a new ambient temperature sensor, which is an inexpensive part, or a wiring repair.

title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
plain: The outside air temperature sensor, usually behind the front grille or bumper, tells the computer how warm it is outside. The computer found a reading that does not make sense compared with other temperature sensors.
symptoms: Wrong outside temperature on the dash
Automatic climate control may not work right

causes.name: Sensor mounted near a heat source or out of place

checks: Check the dash outside temperature reading against the real temperature
Inspect the sensor and its wiring behind the grille or bumper
Test the sensor resistance at a known temperature
fix: Usually a new ambient temperature sensor, which is an inexpensive part, or a wiring repair.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit (Bank 1)
plain: The intake valve control solenoid on bank 1 is an electric valve that adjusts valve timing or lift using oil pressure. The computer found a fault, such as an open circuit, in its circuit.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector at the solenoid

checks: Inspect the solenoid connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec
Command the solenoid with a scan tool and check for a response
fix: Usually a new valve control solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Low (Bank 1)
plain: The intake valve control solenoid on bank 1 is an electric valve that adjusts valve timing or lift using oil pressure. The computer found a voltage that is too low in its circuit.

checks: Inspect the solenoid connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec

title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1)
plain: On turbocharged engines, the charge air cooler (intercooler) cools the boosted air. A sensor measures that air temperature, and the computer found a fault in the circuit from the bank 1 sensor.
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare its reading with other temperature sensors after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new charge air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
plain: On turbocharged engines, the charge air cooler (intercooler) cools the boosted air. A sensor measures that air temperature, and the computer found a reading that does not make sense from the bank 1 sensor.

causes.name: Oil or soot fouling the sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare its reading with other temperature sensors after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new charge air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1)
plain: On turbocharged engines, the charge air cooler (intercooler) cools the boosted air. A sensor measures that air temperature, and the computer found a signal that is too low from the bank 1 sensor.
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring

fix: Usually a new charge air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic (Bank 1)
plain: On turbocharged engines, the charge air cooler (intercooler) cools the boosted air. A sensor measures that air temperature, and the computer found a signal that cuts in and out from the bank 1 sensor.

title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Bank 1/Bank 2 Correlation
plain: On engines with two charge air temperature sensors, the computer compares them. The bank 1 and bank 2 readings disagree by more than they should.

causes.name: One charge air temperature sensor reading wrong
Leak or restriction in one side of the intercooler system

checks: Compare both sensor readings after the engine has sat overnight
Inspect wiring and connectors on both sensors
fix: Usually replacing whichever sensor reads wrong.
